channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Indian Supreme Court treats menstrual health as part of right to life [7/10]
item.description: A ruling treats menstrual health as part of the right to life. A ten-point checklist helps parents assess their daughter's school facilities. (Goodness 7/10: Legal recognition that could improve school facilities for many girls.)

item.title: Teen leads student effort to curb crop burning in West Bengal [7/10]
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Sk Reezaal Arafat leads SATARK, a student climate-tech initiative using satellite data, low-cost sensors and fieldwork to anticipate and reduce crop residue burning. (Goodness 7/10: Local youth action against air pollution, small in scale so far.)

item.title: Passive cooling explored as low-energy option in Colombo [6/10]
item.description: Residents of dense Colombo apartment blocks rely on fans and air conditioning. Sri Lanka is exploring passive cooling methods as an energy-saving alternative, though with costs. (Goodness 6/10: A practical energy-saving idea, still at an exploratory stage.)

item.title: Community leader describes marine conservation in Cambodia [7/10]
item.description: A commune deputy chief on Koh Sdach discusses community-led marine conservation, balancing fishing livelihoods with ecological protection through a community fisheries management area. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led conservation that supports local livelihoods.)

item.title: Family sells 650 acres on East Texas lake for a state park [6/10]
item.description: A multigenerational family sold 650 acres on Lake Palestine to become a state park. The land includes pine woods, bluffs, wetlands and a pecan orchard. (Goodness 6/10: Protected land opens to the public, a local benefit.)

item.title: Ten minutes of daily exercise linked to deeper sleep [6/10]
item.description: A University of Texas at Austin study linked more frequent exercise to more deep sleep. About 10 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity a day showed measurable benefits. (Goodness 6/10: Simple, accessible health finding, but it shows association only.)

item.title: Australia sets a renewable energy record led by rooftop solar [8/10]
item.description: On 22 September solar and wind supplied 80.4 percent of demand on Australia's national grid, with rooftop panels briefly carrying over half the load. The annual renewable share is 44 percent. (Goodness 8/10: Record clean power share, though the annual figure is lower.)

item.title: Changing gait may ease knee arthritis pain [6/10]
item.description: Scientists report that adjusting how a person walks can relieve knee arthritis pain about as well as prescription drugs, and may slow cartilage wear. (Goodness 6/10: A drug-free option for a common condition, though details of evidence are limited.)

item.title: Aldabra giant tortoise count reaches about 180,000 [8/10]
item.description: A survey on Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles counted about 180,000 giant tortoises, the highest figure recorded. The species was once considered endangered. (Goodness 8/10: A recovered, once-endangered species at a record population.)

item.title: Woman electrician keeps power running for a Maharashtra village [6/10]
item.description: Jyoti Sarjerao has worked with the state electricity department and is the person her village calls when the power fails. (Goodness 6/10: Inspiring local profile that breaks a gender barrier.)

item.title: Festival food offerings in Mumbai turned into electricity [7/10]
item.description: About 39 tonnes of leftover food from the Lalbaugcha Raja festival were processed into electricity for a hospital project. (Goodness 7/10: Practical reuse of food waste for a public service.)

item.title: Kenyan children learn chess on sets made from recycled plastic [7/10]
item.description: A community project recycled about 200 kg of plastic into chess sets, teaching children the game while reducing waste. (Goodness 7/10: Small community project combining recycling and education.)

item.title: Carthage Music Days festival features artists from 15 countries [6/10]
item.description: The 11th Carthage Music Days festival ran for a week in Tunis with artists from 15 countries, putting emphasis on the local scene. (Goodness 6/10: A cultural event supporting local musicians.)

item.title: Seed-sized injectable device could treat chronic pain by controlling nerves [6/10]
item.description: A tiny injectable device regulates nerve activity without batteries or wires and could offer a new approach to chronic pain. (Goodness 6/10: Potential relief for many people, but still early research.)

item.title: Sloth bear rescued from India's dancing trade is now thriving [6/10]
item.description: A sloth bear rescued in 2009 from being forced to dance for tourists is reported by a rescue charity to be doing well in its sanctuary home. (Goodness 6/10: Animal rescued from cruelty and now healthy, though it is a single animal.)

item.title: Solar-powered truck processes waste before it reaches landfill [6/10]
item.description: A 22-foot solar-powered mobile unit sorts, shreds and processes waste on site, reducing what goes to landfills. (Goodness 6/10: Practical local waste solution, small scale.)

item.title: Lost model by Trevi Fountain sculptor found in salvage yard [6/10]
item.description: A 27-inch model by sculptor Pietro Bracci was found in a British reclamation yard for about 300 pounds. It was a pitch for a bronze statue of Pope Clement XII. (Goodness 6/10: A pleasant cultural rediscovery with limited wider impact.)

item.title: Ethiopia pursues massive tree-planting campaign to restore forests [6/10]
item.description: Ethiopia is working to replant forests lost to clearing through a large-scale seedling campaign, though challenges remain. (Goodness 6/10: Ambitious restoration with results still to be proven.)

item.title: Women rangers prepare to release Darwin's rheas in Chilean Patagonia [7/10]
item.description: A women-led ranger team is preparing to release 13 Darwin's rheas at Patagonia National Park in Chile to help restore the species. (Goodness 7/10: Local restoration effort for a native bird.)

item.title: Women-led rangers prepare to return Darwin's rheas to Chilean Patagonia [7/10]
item.description: A women-led ranger team is getting ready to release 13 Darwin's rheas into Patagonian habitat as part of a reintroduction effort. (Goodness 7/10: Concrete wildlife restoration led by a local team.)

item.title: Volunteers remove 18,000 kg of plastic from a Mumbai beach in a day [7/10]
item.description: More than 1,500 volunteers cleared 18,000 kilograms of marine plastic from a Mumbai shoreline in one day. (Goodness 7/10: Large community clean-up with visible results.)

item.title: Painting one wind turbine blade black sharply cut bird deaths [7/10]
item.description: A long-term study at a Spanish wind farm found that painting a single turbine blade black greatly reduced annual bird fatalities. (Goodness 7/10: Cheap, practical fix for wind power's wildlife impact.)

item.title: Navi Pillay wins the Nobel Peace Prize [7/10]
item.description: South African-born jurist Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, recognising her work in international justice. (Goodness 7/10: Major recognition for human rights work.)

item.title: Indigenous youth in Ecuador use rap to defend the Amazon [6/10]
item.description: Young Amazonian artists rap in Kichwa and other languages to draw attention to threats to their forests and communities. (Goodness 6/10: Community-driven advocacy and cultural vitality.)

item.title: Victoria, Australia creates three new national parks [8/10]
item.description: About 650 square kilometres of forest in Victoria becomes three national parks, including the large Wombat-Lerderderg park, protecting gliders, owls and other wildlife. (Goodness 8/10: Large new protected habitat for wildlife.)

item.title: Navi Pillay dedicates Nobel Peace Prize to survivors of international crimes [6/10]
item.description: Navi Pillay dedicated her Nobel Peace Prize to survivors of international crimes, highlighting the work of seeking accountability. (Goodness 6/10: Recognition for justice work, though the underlying crimes remain.)

item.title: Australian scientists train seals and sea lions for hearing tests [6/10]
item.description: Researchers at Sydney trained seals and sea lions to take hearing tests, helping assess how ocean noise affects marine mammals. (Goodness 6/10: Useful research for marine animal protection.)

item.title: Ethiopian Airlines to resume flights to Mekelle [6/10]
item.description: Ethiopian Airlines will restart flights to Mekelle, the capital of Tigray, from Sunday. (Goodness 6/10: Restored connection, amid regional tensions.)

item.title: India releases two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the wild [7/10]
item.description: Two captive-bred male Great Indian Bustards were released into Desert National Park in Rajasthan as an experiment to rebuild the critically endangered species. (Goodness 7/10: Hopeful step for a critically endangered bird; outcome uncertain.)

item.title: Study finds local involvement drives conservation success [6/10]
item.description: Researchers examining conservation successes worldwide found that the actions and views of local people mattered more than funding in whether nature recovered. (Goodness 6/10: Useful insight that can improve future projects.)

item.title: Purple bacteria powder matched synthetic fertilizer in crop trials [6/10]
item.description: Dried powder from the purple bacterium Rhodovulum sulfidophilum matched synthetic fertilizers in a two-year trial, hinting at a lower-impact option. (Goodness 6/10: Promising alternative, but early-stage.)

item.title: South African jurist Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize [7/10]
item.description: The Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, a South African judge, for her work promoting peace and international justice. (Goodness 7/10: Major recognition for human rights work.)

item.title: A teenager's project redirects surplus hospital supplies abroad [7/10]
item.description: Project MedBridge, started by 16-year-old Ben Kurian, sends surplus medical supplies from Ohio hospitals to places that need them, rescuing millions of dollars of items. (Goodness 7/10: Practical waste-to-aid model with measurable results.)

item.title: New species of egg-eating snake found in Ethiopian highlands [6/10]
item.description: A new nonvenomous egg-eating snake, the white-throated egg-eater, has been documented in Ethiopia's Harenna Forest. (Goodness 6/10: A new species adds to knowledge and the case for protecting the forest.)

item.title: NASA's Crew-12 astronauts return after eight months in orbit [6/10]
item.description: SpaceX Crew-12 splashed down after about eight months in space, during which they carried out research for future lunar and Mars missions. (Goodness 6/10: Successful mission and return.)

item.title: Goan mother grows ten jars of home recipes into a global business [6/10]
item.description: A woman in Goa who began with ten jars in 2010 now sells traditional Goan masalas and pickles to customers around the world. (Goodness 6/10: A good small-business story for one family and local food traditions.)

item.title: Chennai engineer uses information requests to protect elephants and a lake [7/10]
item.description: A civil engineer in Chennai has used Right to Information requests to expose elephant deaths on rail tracks and help clean a lake, and now explains how others can do the same. (Goodness 7/10: Shows ordinary citizens can drive accountability, though results are local.)

item.title: Floating scarecrow cuts seabird deaths in fishing nets by up to 71 percent [8/10]
item.description: A bird-shaped kite and a spinning, eyed buoy reduced seabird bycatch in Cornish gillnets by up to 71 percent in trials. (Goodness 8/10: Cheap, effective tool that could spread to other fisheries.)

item.title: Jonathan the tortoise, about 194, contributes first epigenome to aging research [6/10]
item.description: Researchers ran genetic tests on Jonathan, an estimated 194-year-old giant tortoise, to learn about aging; it is the first epigenome from such a long-lived animal. (Goodness 6/10: Interesting aging research from a single animal; benefits are still distant.)

item.title: Interpol operation in Latin America leads to hundreds of arrests [7/10]
item.description: Interpol's Operation Madre Tierra across nine countries led to hundreds of arrests and the recovery of over 1,000 animals from wildlife and timber trafficking. (Goodness 7/10: Meaningful enforcement success, though trafficking persists.)

item.title: New York keeps five soccer fields lit late for night workers [6/10]
item.description: New York City Parks extended late-night hours at five soccer fields so people working night shifts can play. (Goodness 6/10: Small but real benefit for a community.)

item.title: Australia's new environmental agency busts wildlife trafficking ring [6/10]
item.description: Australia's National Environmental Protection Agency seized 28 native animals and about A$300,000 in alleged trafficking proceeds in a major operation. (Goodness 6/10: Shows new enforcement capacity working.)

item.title: A strange yellow coral off Costa Rica forms a new evolutionary lineage [6/10]
item.description: Scientists found a yellow coral off Costa Rica that fits no known family, so they created a new one for it, adding to knowledge of deep-sea life. (Goodness 6/10: New knowledge about marine biodiversity.)

item.title: Neighbors in South Dakota free owl tangled in barbed wire [6/10]
item.description: Residents of Spearfish spotted an injured owl caught in barbed wire on private land and gathered to help rescue it. (Goodness 6/10: A small local kindness that saved one animal.)

item.title: Homo erectus fossils in South Africa are 200,000 years older than expected [6/10]
item.description: Fossils from Drimolen Cave, including a skull fragment dated to about 2 million years, push back the known age of Homo erectus. (Goodness 6/10: Notable scientific discovery with no direct practical benefit.)

item.title: Delhi tutor's free classes grow into a movement that cleaned 250 public spaces [7/10]
item.description: Vinay Das began free classes for migrant children in Wazirpur; weekend clean-up drives since 2018 have cleared around 250 parks and streets. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led effort helping children and neighborhoods.)

item.title: Solar grows as an alternative to Nigeria's unreliable grid [6/10]
item.description: Nigeria's power crisis is creating opportunities for solar energy, according to a Business Africa segment. (Goodness 6/10: Clean energy growth, though scale and benefit are unclear.)

item.title: Free kit helps UK communities prepare for emergencies [6/10]
item.description: Prince William launched a free how-to resource that helps local communities build resilience and prepare for emergencies. (Goodness 6/10: A practical, free tool for community preparedness.)

item.title: Twenty kidnapped Nigerian graduates found alive after week-long search [6/10]
item.description: Graduates abducted while travelling to begin national youth service were rescued, authorities confirmed. (Goodness 6/10: Safe return for 20 people, though the kidnapping itself was harmful.)

item.title: More than 14,000 explosives cleared from a Libyan city and nearby farmland [7/10]
item.description: Demining teams backed by the UN and others cleared over 14,000 leftover explosives this year, making homes and farmland safer in a coastal Libyan city. (Goodness 7/10: Real safety gain for a community, though much clearance remains.)

item.title: New York students help improve school lunch by surveying classmates [7/10]
item.description: Through Youth Food Advocates, a Brooklyn student surveyed classmates on why they skipped the cafeteria and what they wanted to eat. (Goodness 7/10: Student-led change that can improve meals for many pupils.)

item.title: Bengaluru's Hesaraghatta grassland becomes a conservation reserve [8/10]
item.description: After nearly two decades of campaigning, Karnataka notified about 5,678 acres of Hesaraghatta grassland as a conservation reserve. (Goodness 8/10: Lasting habitat protection won by citizens near a big city.)

item.title: Berlin volunteers water 900,000 mapped street trees [7/10]
item.description: Berlin's Giess den Kiez app maps about 900,000 street trees and lets 12,000 volunteers coordinate with city crews to water them during heat waves. (Goodness 7/10: A working community model that helps city trees survive heat, though local in scale.)

item.title: London's Oxford Street to close to vehicles this month [6/10]
item.description: Oxford Street will close to all vehicles between Orchard Street and Great Portland Street this month, creating a large pedestrian zone in central London. (Goodness 6/10: Cleaner, safer public space for many people, with effects still to be seen.)

item.title: Stanford molecule turns a cancer driver protein into a self-destruct trigger [6/10]
item.description: Stanford scientists designed a molecule that repurposes a lymphoma-promoting protein to activate cell-death pathways. In mice it eliminated aggressive tumors. (Goodness 6/10: Promising but only shown in mice so far.)

item.title: Satellite tags reveal long journeys of Olive Ridley turtles off Odisha [6/10]
item.description: A three-year Wildlife Institute of India study tracks Olive Ridley turtles with satellite tags and boat surveys. One turtle was followed for 6,719 km. (Goodness 6/10: New data can improve turtle protection.)

item.title: Odisha woman teaches herself tyre repair to support her family [6/10]
item.description: After her husband was injured, Suni Hembram taught herself tyre repair and now runs a roadside repair shop, lifting heavy tyres herself. (Goodness 6/10: Inspiring for one family and community.)

item.title: Profile of Dr Si Padmavati, India's first woman cardiologist [6/10]
item.description: The story covers her work treating underprivileged heart patients, which she continued for long hours into her mid-nineties. (Goodness 6/10: A tribute to lasting service to patients.)

item.title: Raipur family turns forest seeds into chocolate and cosmetic ingredients [6/10]
item.description: A family business in Raipur has grown to about Rs 1,357 crore by processing forest seeds into ingredients for chocolate and cosmetics. (Goodness 6/10: A local enterprise making use of overlooked natural materials.)

item.title: Study maps habitat of the little-known Mishmi takin in Arunachal Pradesh [6/10]
item.description: Researchers combined Indigenous knowledge with camera-trap surveys to map the seasonal movements and habitat use of the Mishmi takin in the Dibang Valley. (Goodness 6/10: Useful conservation knowledge built with local communities.)
